# Entropic Partial Optimal Transport and Partial Gromov–Wasserstein Distance between Gaussian Mixtures

This site accompanies the EPGOT-pMGW paper and publishes its canonical,
executed notebooks for Figures 1–7. The paper defines the experiment. The
generated notebook source is the executable specification and must mirror the
paper exactly. Every figure has one unique PNG output and a JSON sidecar
containing parameters, seeds, fitted inputs, normalization scales, solver
input, matched mass, marginal residuals, runtime, source revisions, coupling
hashes, and output hashes.

## EPOT convention

Figures 1–5 use the extended dummy-point problem (3.1). For source weights
$a$, target weights $b$, normalized component cost $M$, paper penalty
$\lambda$, and entropy parameter $\varepsilon$, the implemented problem is

$$
\min_{\widetilde\omega \in \Pi((a,1),(b,1))}
\left\langle
\begin{pmatrix}
M - 2\lambda & 0 \\
0 & 0
\end{pmatrix},
\widetilde\omega
\right\rangle
+ \varepsilon \sum_{ij}
\widetilde\omega_{ij}(\log \widetilde\omega_{ij}-1).
$$

The reported partial coupling is the real–real block of
$\widetilde\omega$. Thus the public solver input `Lambda` is exactly the
paper's $\lambda$; no factor-of-two conversion is applied. The entropy covers
the entire extended coupling.

## Figures 6–7 penalty scale

Point and mixture costs are each divided by their own pair maximum. The
paper's $\lambda=0.01$ is passed unchanged to both partial solvers on their
respective normalized cost matrices. In the canonical run, PGW and pMGW both
transport $300/350$ mass.

The mixture representation reduces the coupling dimensions from
$300\times350$ to $6\times7$. This is a solver-dimensionality claim, not an
end-to-end speed claim at $N=300$, because fitting the GMM also has a cost.

## Reproducing the site

The exact Python and direct package versions are pinned by `.python-version`,
`pyproject.toml`, and `uv.lock`.

```bash
git submodule update --init --recursive
uv sync --frozen
MPLCONFIGDIR=/tmp/matplotlib \
  uv run python tools/execute_notebooks.py
export QUARTO_PYTHON="$PWD/.venv/bin/python"
quarto render docs
```
